Definition: from G575 and λείχω (to "lick"); to lick clean:--lick.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the parable of the rich man and Lazarus. The beggar lay at the rich man's gate, desiring the crumbs from his table, and the dogs came and licked his sores — the word is the licking clean of wounds by animals, the only comfort Lazarus received on earth.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse, and the dogs show more mercy than the rich man did.
